  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.

  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
  (read `mux.settle_s`).
  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).

  influx-logger kernel.
- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.

- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
  to address unicode issues.

## What this card does not carry

- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
  device card + SAFETIES cell.
- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

}=== ana_cal_md ===
## Run 5 — 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`

Raw map (log R, TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] × BG slow [−1.3, +1.2], 20 × 40 mV, sr1 100 µV; run 4 was the same map aborted at 3 min when the ridge railed at 2 kΩ). **Read:** one dominant CNP ridge (A) running from (V_tg, V_bg) ≈ (+1.0, −1.3) to (−0.3, +0.45), plus a fainter **parallel** ridge (B) ≈ 0.19 V lower in V_tg — the second peak of runs 0–3. Ridge A's resistance is 240 Ω near D ≈ 0 and grows to ~2.4 kΩ at raw D ≈ +0.25 V/nm (saturating beyond), i.e. a D-tunable gap; **not a stacking read** (investigation Step 1 addendum: three candidate parents). Fits (ridge position = V_tg vs V_bg rows, so −slope = c_bg/c_tg): ridge A in the operating window |V_bg| < 0.5: slope −0.773 (rms 19 mV); high-D rows: −0.763 (rms 6 mV); ridge B: −0.69 (8 rows, rms 13 mV). **Calibration:** ratio c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data-calibrated; prior 0.864, −11 % — plausible hBN-thickness error, not a transposition); c_tg anchored at the 9.5 nm prior (absolute scale = geometry prior, pending a lever-arm check); n_offset = −0.089×10¹²; **D_offset from the R_CNP(D) symmetry** (vertex of the ridge-A resistance minimum, ≈ +0.012 raw) — the one feature that physically locates D = 0. Region B is electron-doped by 0.43×10¹² relative to A: a series-mosaic confound (same template expected, 13 % higher n at the fan density — extra tones at ×1.13). Realized D = 0 window inside the validators: **n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹²** (TG-limited on both ends). Channel arithmetic: R = (sr1_X/1)/(sr0_X/−1e6).
=== md_spot_e ===
## HERA — Step 3: SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = +3.2×10¹² at D = 0, B 0 → 10 T

Calibration from run 5 (ana): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior), n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) symmetry). The D = 0 line inside the validators spans n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹², so the electron side is the high-|n| side: spot at **n = +3.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (+0.984, +1.166) V, 16 mV under the TG limit. **Feasibility (Step 2, model table):** F_L = 33.1 T; ABAB pair ≈ 7.5 / 25.6 T (m* 0.028 / 0.061 mₑ), ABCA singleton 33.1 T (m* 0.074); the heavy-ABAB-vs-ABCA split is 7.5 T. Grid: uniform in B (blocking magnet) — 50 mT from 0 to 1 T (MR background only; LK at T_e ≈ 8 K kills m* = 0.06 below ~1.5 T), **10 mT from 1 to 10 T**; 921 points. Dwell: `delay = 0` — each `magnet.field` set blocks through the ramp plus the driver's 3 s settle = 10 τ at τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB, i.e. the lock-in is at the settling floor at every point. Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).
=== md_spot_h ===
## HERA — Step 3b: SdH spot check, hole side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = −1.2×10¹² at D = 0, riding the magnet 10 → 0.3 T

Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) ends at 10 T with the gates at the spot. The investigation takes both signs (no side prior); the hole side of the D = 0 line reaches only n = −1.27×10¹² (TG −0.3 V limit), so the spot sits at **n = −1.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (−0.280, −0.463) V. Feasibility (model): F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB pair ≈ 5.3 / 7.1 T (the near-CNP semimetal regime, tones close and balanced — the recipe's stated low-|n| exception), ABCA 12.4 T with m* ≈ 1 mₑ — LK-dead at this rig's T_e ≈ 8 K. **Coverage trade, stated:** this is a cheap preview, not a decisive read — it costs ~35 min over the bare 10 → 0 T ramp the session needs anyway, and a null here is resolvability-limited, not evidence. Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

```python
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")

assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)

s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_spot); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_spot)
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
```

"""cnp-and-dline-calibration on gatemap run 5: per-row ridge extraction (two ridges), ratio fit on the
operating window near D = 0, offsets, closure check, realized D = 0 n-window; writes cal params to JSON."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5
g = fan_grids(f"data/{rid}"); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} rows x {g.nfast}; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; prior c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}")

# ridge extraction: per row, up to two peaks; track continuity from the high-|D| end where ridge A is unambiguous
pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)
dist = pts[:, 1] - np.polyval(cfA0, pts[:, 0])
ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

print("--- ridge A (main) ---")
cfA_all = fit(ridgeA, -2, 2, "A all rows")
cfA_hiD = fit(ridgeA, -2, -0.6, "A high-D rows")
cfA_op = fit(ridgeA, -0.5, 0.5, "A operating window |Vbg|<0.5")
print("--- ridge B (parallel, lower Vtg) ---")
cfB_all = fit(ridgeB, -2, 2, "B all rows")
cfB_op = fit(ridgeB, -0.5, 0.5, "B operating window")

# calibration: anchor c_tg at the prior (single hBN dielectric, better constrained), set c_bg from the operating-window ratio
cf = cfA_op if cfA_op is not None else cfA_all
ratio = -cf[0]; c_tg = c_tg0; c_bg = ratio * c_tg
n0, _ = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg); n_offset = -n0
nA_ridge = calc_nD(np.polyval(cf, ridgeA[:, 0]), ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0]
print(f"\nCALIBRATION (ridge A, operating window): ratio {ratio:.3f} (prior {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}, {100*(ratio/(c_bg0/c_tg0)-1):+.0f}%), "
      f"c_tg {c_tg:.3e} F/m2 (prior anchor), c_bg {c_bg:.3e}; n_offset {n_offset:+.4f}e12; closure max|n| on fitted line {np.abs(nA_ridge).max():.3f}e12")

=== hera-analysis ===
# `hera.analysis` API Reference

Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.

Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.

A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).

---

## Loading runs

### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.

### `Run` (dataclass)
`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.

| member | description |
|---|---|
| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
| `tags` | comments after the first |
| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
| `rows` | row count |

Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
with `col_indices` + `col_at`.

### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
Lines with no data are omitted.

---

## Lock-in channel / gain model

Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is

`marginal` (peak SNR < `marginal_mult`×threshold; excluded from the headline) /

> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)

> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density

(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:


- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.

1	# vti-02 / VTI — session brief
2	
3	*Session context for the agent-driven measurement session on the VTI. This file is
4	the `hera-tactical` agent's first message — it names the goal and carries the
5	session-specific facts. Protocol, gates, and boundaries live in your agent prompt;
6	the measurement method is yours to derive from the goal, the cards, and the API
7	reference; this brief does not restate protocol.*
8	
9	## Contract — autonomous
10	
11	This session runs **autonomous (E1)**. After the operator gives the grant (below)
12	**you execute measure cells yourself**; you are not waiting for a keystroke per cell.
13	The operator supervises, is reachable on Slack, and can stop any running cell or
14	withdraw the grant at any time. The deployed measure-notebook policy (`append_exec`)
15	is the hard gate on execution; the grant is the protocol gate on top.
16	
17	## Autonomy — this session's parameters
18	
19	- **Mode:** E1 (autonomous).
20	- **Grant (conditional on VERIFY):** after setup (gate A) and SAFETIES (gate B)
21	  are operator-run and green, you author and land the VERIFY cell; the operator
22	  may then say **"go for autonomy"** without running it. Your first E1 acts are
23	  the read-only kernel-binding probe, then executing VERIFY yourself. The cell's
24	  last output line is the verdict — `VERIFY: ALL GREEN` or `VERIFY: FAIL <item>`
25	  — and the grant keys on that printed line, not your reading of the cell. On
26	  ALL GREEN, record grant + verdict in `session_notes.md` and engage. On any
27	  FAIL, or a missing verdict line, the grant is void: drop to E0, notify the
28	  operator, resume only on explicit re-grant. No measure cell executes before
29	  the green verdict. Until the grant you are in E0 (you propose, the operator
30	  runs).
31	- **Operator + notify:** `Zack — hera-notify --user ZACKG`.
32	- **Auto:** in-envelope measure cells (sweeps, gate sets) that stay inside the
33	  committed validators and pass their precondition reads; field moves within the
34	  device-card field cap; temperature moves via `heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`
35	  within the device-card T cap, honoring the rig card's thermometry and settling
36	  facts (read them before the first elevated-T segment).
37	- **Consent-gated:** any deviation from `ratio = 0.95` in `set_both`.
38	- **Consent-gated (Si):** the Si (DC205) ramp — keep the gate-safe pacing;
39	  `dc205.ramp_rate` is consent-gated (never raise without operator consent).
40	- **Session-banned** (never, regardless of grant): any change to a safety surface —
41	  the SAFETIES validators, the gate operating limits, the field cap, or the
42	  T-setpoint cap; and the banned activities below.
43	- **Withdraw / drop:** the operator can withdraw the grant → you revert to E0. You are

45	  stop/E0 drop, resume autonomous execution **only on an explicit E1 re-grant**.

48	
49	**Determine the stacking order of vti-02 (tetralayer graphene): ABAB (Bernal) vs
50	ABCA (rhombohedral) vs ABCB (mixed)** — an independent, evidence-cited,
51	region-resolved call (or a calibrated "cannot tell"), per the output contract below.
52	
53	## Method
54	
55	Derive the measurement plan from the goal,
56	`device_card.md`, `rig_card.md`, the API reference under
57	`~/measurement_env/docs/api/` (`measureme.md`, `hera-analysis.md`, `drivers.md`,
58	`sharpelab-nb-drivers.md`), and the data this session produces. Before the first

73

*Session context for the agent-driven measurement session on the VTI. This file is
the `hera-tactical` agent's first message — it names the goal and carries the
session-specific facts. Protocol, gates, and boundaries live in your agent prompt;
the measurement method is yours to derive from the goal, the cards, and the API
reference; this brief does not restate protocol.*

## Contract — autonomous

This session runs **autonomous (E1)**. After the operator gives the grant (below)
**you execute measure cells yourself**; you are not waiting for a keystroke per cell.
The operator supervises, is reachable on Slack, and can stop any running cell or
withdraw the grant at any time. The deployed measure-notebook policy (`append_exec`)
is the hard gate on execution; the grant is the protocol gate on top.

## Autonomy — this session's parameters

- **Mode:** E1 (autonomous).
- **Grant (conditional on VERIFY):** after setup (gate A) and SAFETIES (gate B)
  are operator-run and green, you author and land the VERIFY cell; the operator
  may then say **"go for autonomy"** without running it. Your first E1 acts are
  the read-only kernel-binding probe, then executing VERIFY yourself. The cell's
  last output line is the verdict — `VERIFY: ALL GREEN` or `VERIFY: FAIL <item>`
  — and the grant keys on that printed line, not your reading of the cell. On
  ALL GREEN, record grant + verdict in `session_notes.md` and engage. On any
  FAIL, or a missing verdict line, the grant is void: drop to E0, notify the
  operator, resume only on explicit re-grant. No measure cell executes before
  the green verdict. Until the grant you are in E0 (you propose, the operator
  runs).
- **Operator + notify:** `Zack — hera-notify --user ZACKG`.
- **Auto:** in-envelope measure cells (sweeps, gate sets) that stay inside the
  committed validators and pass their precondition reads; field moves within the
  device-card field cap; temperature moves via `heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`
  within the device-card T cap, honoring the rig card's thermometry and settling
  facts (read them before the first elevated-T segment).

- **Consent-gated (Si):** the Si (DC205) ramp — keep the gate-safe pacing;
  `dc205.ramp_rate` is consent-gated (never raise without operator consent).
- **Session-banned** (never, regardless of grant): any change to a safety surface —
  the SAFETIES validators, the gate operating limits, the field cap, or the
  T-setpoint cap; and the banned activities below.
- **Withdraw / drop:** the operator can withdraw the grant → you revert to E0. You are
  free to stop, notify, and drop to E0 on any device- or rig-safety concern. After any
  stop/E0 drop, resume autonomous execution **only on an explicit E1 re-grant**.

**Determine the stacking order of vti-02 (tetralayer graphene): ABAB (Bernal) vs
ABCA (rhombohedral) vs ABCB (mixed)** — an independent, evidence-cited,
region-resolved call (or a calibrated "cannot tell"), per the output contract below.

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

"""SdH spot checks runs 6/7: raw R(B), onset, FFT tones."""
import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, current_channel, sdh_fft, sdh_onset

for rid in (6, 7):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    chs = resolve_channels(r.meta); cur = current_channel(chs)
    B = r.col('magnet_field') if 'magnet_field' in r.cols else r.col_at(1)
    I = r.col_at(cur.idx) / cur.gain
    v = [c for c in chs if not c.is_current]
    print(f"=== run {rid}: {r.rows} rows, cols {r.cols}")
    print(f"  B {B.min():.3f} -> {B.max():.3f}; I med {np.median(I):.3e} A; voltage chans {[c.cid for c in v]}")
    ch = [c for c in v if c.cid == 'sr1'][0]
    R = np.abs((r.col_at(ch.idx) / ch.gain) / I)
    print(f"  R(sr1): {R.min():.1f} - {R.max():.1f} Ohm; R@Bmin {R[np.argmin(B)]:.1f}, R@Bmax {R[np.argmax(B)]:.1f}")
    o = np.argsort(B); Bs, Rs = B[o], R[o]
    sens = r.meta['measurement_config'].get('sr1_sens')
    fs = (sens / np.median(I)) if sens else None
    print(f"  sr1_sens {sens}, full-scale R ~ {fs:.0f} Ohm" if fs else "  no sens")
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(Rs, Bs, r_full_scale=fs)
        print(on.summary())
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  sdh_onset FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    m = Bs > 1.0
    f, sp = sdh_fft(Rs[m][:, None], Bs[m])
    s = sp[0]
    k = np.argsort(s)[::-1][:12]
    print(f"  FFT (B>1T, df={1/(1/Bs[m].min()-1/Bs[m].max()):.2f} T): top peaks (T, rel amp):")
    seen=[]
    for i in np.argsort(s)[::-1]:
        if f[i] < 2: continue
        if any(abs(f[i]-x) < 2.0 for x in seen): continue
        seen.append(f[i]); print(f"     F = {f[i]:7.2f} T   amp {s[i]/s.max():.3f}")
        if len(seen) >= 8: break
    np.save(f"hera_scratch/spot{rid}_BR.npy", np.vstack([Bs, Rs]))
EOF

```python
def spoints(a, b, c):
    return np.linspace(a, b, c)


def sanitize_tg_bg(vtg_vec, vbg_vec, tg_lims, bg_lims):
    """
    Given a list of tg and bg voltages, removes any points which are outside tg_lims and bg_lims
    """
    vtg_new_vec = []
    vbg_new_vec = []
    for ind in range(len(vtg_vec)):
        vtg, vbg = vtg_vec[ind], vbg_vec[ind]
        if vtg < tg_lims[0] or vtg > tg_lims[1] or vbg < bg_lims[0] or vbg > bg_lims[1]:
            pass
        else:
            vtg_new_vec.append(vtg)
            vbg_new_vec.append(vbg)
    return np.array(vtg_new_vec), np.array(vbg_new_vec)
```

# === Landau fan (`landau-fan`): R_xx(B, n) at D = 0 — the stacking discriminator (plan step 5) ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-fit, absolute scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B| < 1: fan starts low), "
      f"V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), nplci tg/bg = {k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()} (1/1), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 1.0 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1, "gate-current nplci not reset to 1"
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()
# validators still the committed ones (gate B contract; read, never write)
assert (k_2400_tg.volt.vals._min_value, k_2400_tg.volt.vals._max_value) == (TG_MIN, TG_MAX)
assert (k_2400_bg.volt.vals._min_value, k_2400_bg.volt.vals._max_value) == (BG_MIN, BG_MAX)
assert magnet.field.vals._max_value == B_SESSION_CAP

# --- fast axis: the D = 0 line, n = -1.24 ... +3.24e12 (TG-limited at both ends, >= 5 mV inside the validators) ---
N_FAST = 91
n_vec = np.linspace(-1.24, +3.24, N_FAST)                      # 1e12 cm^-2
Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec = calc_gate_voltages(n_vec, 0.0, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec = sanitize_tg_bg(Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec, tg_lims, bg_lims)
assert len(Vtg_vec) == len(Vbg_vec) == N_FAST, (len(Vtg_vec), len(Vbg_vec))   # nothing clipped out
assert Vtg_vec.min() > TG_MIN + 0.004 and Vtg_vec.max() < TG_MAX - 0.004
assert Vbg_vec.min() > BG_MIN + 0.004 and Vbg_vec.max() < BG_MAX - 0.004
_nchk, _Dchk = calc_nD(Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert np.abs(_Dchk).max() < 1e-9, _Dchk
print(f"fast: n {n_vec[0]:+.2f} -> {n_vec[-1]:+.2f}e12 in {N_FAST} pts ({(n_vec[1]-n_vec[0])*1e3:.1f}e9 step) at D = 0; "
      f"Vtg {Vtg_vec.min():+.4f}..{Vtg_vec.max():+.4f}, Vbg {Vbg_vec.min():+.4f}..{Vbg_vec.max():+.4f} V")

# --- slow axis: uniform in 1/B (SdH is periodic in 1/B) with a 0.40 T cap on dB so the
#     high-field end stays readable as a fan. d(1/B) = 0.0105 -> F_Nyquist = 48 T (F_L ~ 33.5 T). ---
B_LO, B_HI, D_INV, DB_MAX = 0.7, 10.0, 0.0105, 0.40
_b = [B_LO]
while _b[-1] < B_HI - 1e-9:
    _nxt = 1.0 / (1.0 / _b[-1] - D_INV) if (1.0 / _b[-1] - D_INV) > 0 else B_HI
    _b.append(min(_nxt, _b[-1] + DB_MAX, B_HI))
B_vec = np.round(np.array(_b), 4)
assert np.all(np.diff(B_vec) > 0) and B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
_dinv = -np.diff(1.0 / B_vec)
print(f"slow: {len(B_vec)} B rows {B_vec[0]:.2f} -> {B_vec[-1]:.2f} T; dB {np.diff(B_vec).min():.4f}..{np.diff(B_vec).max():.3f} T; "
      f"F_Nyquist {1/(2*_dinv.max()):.0f} T; dF = {1/(1/B_vec.min()-1/B_vec.max()):.2f} T")

FAST_DELAY, SLOW_DELAY = 1.0, 3.0   # tau = 0.3 s @ 24 dB/oct -> 1.0 s is ~1 fast-point of lag/smoothing (= 0.05e12 in n)
I_TRIP = 1e-9                       # gate-leak trip; observed flyback transients peak ~0.2 nA
assert sr1.time_constant() == 0.3 and sr1.filter_slope() == 24, (sr1.time_constant(), sr1.filter_slope())

# Fixed sensitivity for the whole fan (no autorange mid-row): 100 uV = 10 kOhm FS at 10 nA.
# Spot checks peaked at 590 Ohm (5.8 % FS); the headroom is for the CNP columns at high B.
sr1.sensitivity(100e-6)
_I = abs(sr1.amplitude() / meas_config["bias_resistor"])
print(f"drive {sr1.amplitude()} V / {meas_config['bias_resistor']:.0e} Ohm = {_I*1e9:.2f} nA; "
      f"sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V = {sr1.sensitivity()/_I:.0f} Ohm FS; tau {sr1.time_constant()} s @ {sr1.filter_slope()} dB/oct; "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V")
print(f"priced: {len(B_vec)} rows x ({N_FAST} x {FAST_DELAY+0.17:.2f} s + {SLOW_DELAY+3.5:.1f} s) + "
      f"{(B_HI-abs(_B0))/0.137/60:.2f} h ramp = {(len(B_vec)*(N_FAST*(FAST_DELAY+0.17)+SLOW_DELAY+3.5+3)+(B_HI-abs(_B0))/0.137*60)/3600:.2f} h nominal")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = (f"landau-fan: B slow {B_vec[0]}-{B_vec[-1]} T ({len(B_vec)} rows, uniform 1/B d=0.0105, dB cap 0.40 T); "
                  f"(Vtg,Vbg) fast along D = 0, n {n_vec[0]:+.2f}..{n_vec[-1]:+.2f}e12 ({N_FAST}); sr1 sens 100 uV; run-5 cal")
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan')
s.add_comment(f'D = 0 fan: fast (Vtg, Vbg) along D = 0, n {n_vec[0]:+.2f} -> {n_vec[-1]:+.2f}e12 cm^-2 ({N_FAST} pts, '
              f'{(n_vec[1]-n_vec[0])*1e3:.1f}e9 step), Vtg {Vtg_vec.min():+.4f}..{Vtg_vec.max():+.4f} / Vbg {Vbg_vec.min():+.4f}..{Vbg_vec.max():+.4f}; '
              f'slow B {B_vec[0]:.2f} -> {B_vec[-1]:.2f} T, {len(B_vec)} rows uniform in 1/B (d(1/B) = {D_INV}, dB capped {DB_MAX} T), '
              f'F_Nyquist {1/(2*_dinv.max()):.0f} T, dF {1/(1/B_vec.min()-1/B_vec.max()):.2f} T; sr1 100 uV (10 kOhm FS); '
              f'fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s (tau 0.3 s / 24 dB); T_sample {_T0:.3f} K; Vsi = 0; '
              f'cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_vec[0]); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_vec[0])
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B(slow), Vtg(fast), Vbg(fast), T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)
s.plot('time', T_sample); s.plot('time', sr1.P); s.plot('time', sr0.P)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, Vtg={float(data[2]):+.4f}, Vbg={float(data[3]):+.4f}: "
              f"|I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

try:
    s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec],
                     slow_delay=SLOW_DELAY, fast_delay=FAST_DELAY)
finally:

**Why this, now (plan step 5).** The spot checks (runs 6, 7) established that this
device gives fully developed Landau levels — minima reach R ≈ 0, SNR 40–120, onset at
0.3–0.7 T — but a *single* density cannot separate the competing readings of run 6's
tone set {7.1, 14.1, 22.2, 29.5 T}: it is equally consistent with a **harmonic ladder
of one 7.4 T fundamental**, with a **two-surface pair {7.1, 22.2}** (minority fraction
x ≈ 0.24), and with **{4.2, 29.5}** (x ≈ 0.13, and the only pair whose sum matches
F_L = 33.1 T). Those three readings map onto three different stackings. A fan resolves
them because it measures F at *every* density at once.

**The physics being tested.** Min–MacDonald chiral decomposition of a 4-layer stack:
**ABAB → 2 + 2** (two bilayer-like Fermi surfaces), **ABCA → 4** (one chirality-4
surface), **ABCB → 1 + 3** (a Dirac-like minority pocket plus a rhombohedral-trilayer
one). Each surface gives F_i = n_i·h/4e, so the **calibration-free** observable is the
set of fractions x_i = F_i / ΣF_j — our absolute n scale is still the c_tg geometry
prior, so fractions, not absolute frequencies, carry the verdict. At n = +3.24×10¹²
(F_L = 33.5 T) the models predict: **ABCA {33.5}**, **ABAB {9.2, 24.3}** (x = 0.28),
**ABCB {2.5, 31.0}** (x = 0.07). Three discriminations come out of one map:
(i) **F_i(n) slopes** — a real second surface has dF₂/dn = x₂·h/4e, whereas a harmonic
has dF/dn exactly k× the fundamental's, and over the full n range those diverge by
≫ δF; (ii) **Landau-line families** — one uniformly spaced family converging on the CNP
(single surface) vs two incommensurate families with crossings (two surfaces);
(iii) **e–h asymmetry and a D = 0 CNP gap**, the inversion-breaking ABCB tell. Free
bonus: where the lines converge validates the run-5 (n, D) calibration.

**Grid.** Slow axis is B (the rate-limited axis): **0.7 → 10 T, 132 rows uniform in
1/B** (d(1/B) = 0.0105 → F_Nyquist = 47 T, comfortably above F_L ≈ 33.5 T and above the
~37–40 T implied by run 6's high-field minima spacing), with **ΔB capped at 0.40 T** so
the high-field end stays readable as a fan rather than collapsing to 7 sparse rows —
the cap only ever makes the 1/B spacing finer, so Nyquist is untouched. Resolution
δF = 1/(1/0.7 − 1/10) = **0.75 T**. Fast axis is the **D = 0 line, n = −1.24 …
+3.24×10¹², 91 points** (44.8×10⁹ step), co-swept (V_tg, V_bg) via `multimegasweep`;
both ends are TG-limited with ≥ 5 mV inside the committed validators. `fast_delay` =
1.0 s is priced against the operator-set τ = 0.3 s at 24 dB/oct: it is ~1 fast-point of
lag/smoothing (≈ 0.05×10¹² in n), which is ≪ the ν = 4 gap width (0.097×10¹²·B) for
B ≳ 2 T. sr1 at 100 µV = 10 kΩ FS — the spot checks peaked at 590 Ω (5.8 % FS); the
headroom is for the CNP columns at high B.

**Coverage trade (stated).** The hole side stops at n = −1.24×10¹² while the electron
side reaches +3.24×10¹²: the D = 0 line runs out of top gate at V_tg = −0.3 V. Deeper
hole density is not reachable this session — it would need the TG limit moved (banned)
or the Si gate (standalone Si survey banned), so the e–h asymmetry read is qualified to
|n| ≤ 1.24×10¹². Low-B rows under-sample n for a *visual* fan (at B = 1 T the ν = 4 gap
is only 1.9 fast points wide); those rows are carried by the 1/B FFT, not by eye.

**Preconditions the cell asserts (eyeball these):** T_sample 1.0–1.5 K with a live
thermometry logfile, |B| < 1 T at entry, V_si = 0, gate nplci 1/1, PS heater on and
output enabled, and the three committed validators unchanged (read-only re-check of the
gate B contract). Gate-leak trip at 1 nA (flyback transients peak ~0.2 nA).

**Checkpoints.** (1) **First 2 rows (~12 min):** R across the n line at 0.7 T — CNP
visible near n = 0, no rail against 10 kΩ, leak < 1 nA, phase sane; the cheapest kill.
(2) **~1.7 h (B ≈ 1.0 T)** and (3) **~3.5 h (B ≈ 2.0 T):** re-form the partial fan and
run `sdh_fft` on the landed rows — tone count and whether F(n) is already splitting into
more than one linear family. (4) **~5.0 h (B ≈ 5.2 T):** the visual fan lines. Abort
criteria: a railed or dead channel, a leak trip, or no resolvable second family *and*
no single clean family by checkpoint 3 (then the read is resolution-limited and the
remaining budget is better spent on `lk-mass`).

**Ends at 10 T with the gates parked at 0 V** — the field is deliberately left high so
the follow-up (step 6: `lk-mass` T-dependence, or a D-dependence slice) rides it down
rather than re-traversing.
